baseline_models.focus_anchor: The coordinated nominal chain `Ad, Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot.
baseline_models.mechanism: The proper-name branch fixes `Ad as a tribe, while the brotherhood branch marks the last entry by relationship. Repeated coordination places a tribe, a ruler-name, and an affiliated group on one corporate roster.

activation_trace.role: The tribe-name branch fixes `Ad as a historical corporate label in the coordinated roster.
Brotherhood and kinship supply the relational label by which Lot's associated group enters the roster.

changed_reading.before: Three names or labels are merely juxtaposed.
changed_reading.after: The ayah is a deliberately mixed corporate roster whose entries can be represented by tribe, political center, or relational group.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The plural relational noun إخوان attached to Lot.
baseline_models.mechanism: The inventory allows both kinship and a tether or bond. The phrase can therefore name a brother-like affiliation organized around Lot, without requiring that only biological siblinghood be in view.

activation_trace.role: The kinship branch supplies the ordinary brotherhood relation and its extension toward friendship.
The tether branch recasts brotherhood functionally as a bond that holds an affiliated group together.

changed_reading.before: The phrase points only to Lot's literal brothers.
changed_reading.after: The phrase may designate people held together by a brother-like social bond around Lot.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The written form and supplied root inventory of عَادٌ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The proper-name branch remains primary, but the same focus inventory also supplies return after departure. The tribal name can carry a latent recurrence or return echo without ceasing to be a name.

activation_trace.role: The tribe branch contains the reading within the proper name `Ad.
Return after departure supplies a secondary audible or root-level echo of recurrence.

changed_reading.before: `Ad functions only as an opaque ethnonym.
changed_reading.after: `Ad remains the ethnonym while tentatively sounding a return-or-recurrence motif.

context_deltas.mechanism: The whole-surah sequence moves from disputed return from dust, through emergence from dead land, to the returning person and final destination. That sustained motion reactivates the focus inventory's return branch inside the name `Ad, making the cataloged past participate in the surah's forward return arc.

activation_trace.role: The tribe branch preserves `Ad as the literal roster entry rather than replacing the name with an abstraction.
Return after departure is the focus-side branch reactivated by the surah-wide movement.
Return and restoration introduce the disputed motion that the name's return branch can echo.
Passage outward supplies the emergence stage in the return mechanism.
Return to a place makes recurrent return a human disposition later in the surah.
Becoming toward the final destination closes the return trajectory.

structural_cues: The activators span 50:3, 50:11, 50:32, and 50:43, so the effect belongs to the whole-surah package rather than only the adjacent catalog.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies several return, emergence, and destination branches; I infer that their repetition reactivates the same branch under the proper name `Ad. The live alternative is that `Ad remains semantically opaque and the recurrence is only formal.

changed_reading.before: The ayah interrupts resurrection discourse with a detached list of past names.
changed_reading.after: The `Ad entry remains historical but also becomes a lexical hinge joining past recurrence to the surah's promised return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The flanking ayat label groups as a people and as companions; the focus substitutes tribe-name, ruler-name, and brothers. The closing totalizer then assigns every entry the same rejection of messengers and the same binding threat. The focus line is therefore the middle panel of a taxonomy of corporate affiliation, not a self-contained name list.

activation_trace.role: The tribe branch contributes one way a rejecting collectivity is named.
Brotherhood contributes a second, relational way a collectivity is named.
A people or human group supplies the first flanking social category.
Companionship and sustained association supply another flanking affiliation category.
Total enclosure gathers all differently labeled entries under one judgment.
Contradiction of truth supplies the shared action that resolves the otherwise verbless roster.
The messenger and message branch identifies the common object of the groups' rejection.
Necessary, binding realization turns the catalog's shared act into a common consequence.
Threat directed toward harm supplies the consequence that closes the catalog.

structural_cues: Ayat 50:12-14 form one coordinated sequence: two catalog lines without a shared finite predicate are closed by the totalizing clause in 50:14.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies alternating group labels and a final totalizer, rejection, and threat; I let that closure back-propagate over the focus line and infer a taxonomy of affiliation. A live alternative is a simpler additive list with no special force in the label variation.

changed_reading.before: 50:13 is an autonomous list of three historical labels.
changed_reading.after: 50:13 is the center of a three-ayah social taxonomy whose diverse corporate forms are equalized by one rejection and one consequence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The catalog first compresses people into brotherhood, tribe, and ruler; later every self arrives with a driver and witness, and an attached companion speaks. The later judgment scene decomposes collective solidarity into an accountable self plus its attached relations, so إخوان no longer offers anonymous shelter inside a group.

activation_trace.role: Brotherhood supplies the collective solidarity that the later sequence tests at individual scale.
The bond or tether branch makes the group's internal attachment functionally visible.
The self as the very individual thing supplies the unit to which the corporate roster is later reduced.
Driving or conducting gives each self a directed, noncollective arrival.
Presence with witnessing makes individual exposure rather than group cover the operative condition.
An attached companion preserves relation, but now as a companion paired with an individual rather than a protective collective.

structural_cues: After the corporate catalog, 50:16-29 repeatedly narrows the field to a human self, each self, and a singular companion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the scale shift from named collectivities to each self with attached figures; I infer that this shift functionally dissolves collective anonymity. It need not deny real social kinship, and the sequence does not explicitly state that brotherhood itself is broken.

changed_reading.before: The brothers of Lot are accountable only as an undifferentiated corporate bloc.
changed_reading.after: Their brotherhood is a real bond, yet the whole-surah movement exposes each member as a self accompanied into individual accounting.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet maps the transgressor occurrence not only to boundary-crossing but also to the same ع و د inventory carried by `Ad, specifically habit and repeated practice. This permits `Ad to become an exploratory emblem of recurrent, habituated overstepping inside the catalog, while the tribe-name branch remains literal.

activation_trace.role: The proper-name branch contains the model: the surface still names the tribe `Ad.
Habit, practice, and persistence supply the focus-side mechanism of repeated conduct.
Crossing a limit and wrongdoing supply the literal conduct attributed after the catalog.
The packet's non-dominant mapping routes that conduct into the same habit and persistence branch activated under `Ad.

structural_cues: The agent-level characterization in 50:24-26 follows the corporate catalog and converts collective rejection into recurring dispositions.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a shared mapped branch between the focus name and the later transgressor; I infer a thematic echo of practiced transgression, not an etymology or historical definition of `Ad. The proper-name-only reading remains fully live.

changed_reading.before: `Ad contributes identity alone to the list.
changed_reading.after: `Ad still names the tribe but can exploratorily resonate with overstepping that has become habitual and recurrent.

context_deltas.mechanism: A secondary focus mapping places عَادٌ in the counting inventory, including counted recurrence. The warning root and the ready-at-hand root also map into that inventory, while day supplies bounded time. Together they recast the historical roster as countable, prepared installments in a timed warning.

activation_trace.role: The secondary focus target contributes the act of counting the rostered item.
Counted time and scheduled recurrence make the item one possible installment in a repeated pattern.
The dominant warning branch supplies the threatened event governing the roster.
The split mapping links that warning to counted time and recurrence.
Preparation and equipment supply the sense that each reckoning is already made ready.
A bounded duration gives the recurrent warning its explicit temporal frame.

structural_cues: The catalog closes with warning in 50:14, readiness appears in 50:18, and the day of warning is named in 50:20.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies shared split-root branches of counting, preparation, and scheduled recurrence; I infer that they can organize the names as installments in a timed pattern. The materially live alternative is that these mappings are lexicographic possibilities with no discourse-level connection.

changed_reading.before: The list is an unstructured accumulation of past groups.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, each listed group is a counted precedent in a prepared and temporally bounded recurrence of warning.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it transfers a material cord and the act of binding into a social noun. It remains anchored in the focus inventory's explicit tether branch and in exact whole-surah cord and pairing branches; downstream prose should present it only as a possible structural resonance, never as a replacement lexical meaning for إخوان or as a claim of literal restraint.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The الآخية or tether branch supplied for focus word إخوان.

activation_trace.role: Ordinary brotherhood keeps the outlier attached to the actual relational noun.
A tether or fastening supplies the focus-side image of social attachment.
A stretched cord that binds or leads gives the material geometry of attachment.
Joining one thing to another converts the cord geometry into relational pairing later in the surah.

changed_reading.before: Brothers are simply members of a named kin category.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the brothers form a tethered affiliation network whose very bonds make it a coherent accountable unit.

strongest_changes: The closure in 50:14 turns the focus into the middle panel of a three-ayah taxonomy of corporate affiliation and supplies its shared act and consequence.
The whole-surah return, emergence, returner, and destination sequence reactivates a latent return branch under the proper name `Ad.
The later movement to each self, driver, witness, and companion revises collective brotherhood into a bond whose members remain individually exposed.
summary.what_was_special: The focus is extremely short and largely nominal, so the strongest activation came from whole-surah sequence and from the packet's split mappings: a proper name stayed literal while acquiring return, habit, and counted-recurrence resonances, and a kin term acquired both social and material bond mechanics.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether a proper ethnonym such as `Ad can sustain root-level return resonance beyond formal wordplay.
Whether إخوان here favors literal kinship, broad affiliation, or both.
Whether the non-dominant mappings to habit and counting are discourse activations or only lexicographic accidents.
